title: “Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward…
content: “Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward form … toward feeling … toward perception … toward formations, dwell often in disenchantment toward consciousness. One who dwells often in disenchantment toward form … toward consciousness fully understands form … feeling … perception … formations … fully understands consciousness. One who fully understands form, fully understands feeling, fully understands perception, fully understands formations, fully understands consciousness, is freed from form, freed from feeling, freed from perception, freed from formations, freed from consciousness, freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is freed from suffering.”

title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
content: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’”

title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
content:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

title: “One who has cut off craving, Without remainder, Dried up the swift stream — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like a serpent…
content:
“One who has cut off craving,
Without remainder,
Dried up the swift stream —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who has destroyed conceit,
Without remainder,
As a great flood destroys a fragile reed —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: “Monks, there are these three elements of escape. What three? The escape from sensual pleasures — that is renunciation. The escape from form — that…
content:
“Monks, there are these three elements of escape. What three? The escape from sensual pleasures — that is renunciation. The escape from form — that is the formless. And as to whatever has come to be, is conditioned, dependently arisen, its escape is its cessation. These, monks, are the three elements of escape.

Knowing the escape from sensual pleasures,
And transcending all forms,
Always ardent, calming all conditioned things —
That monk sees rightly.

From that, being thus liberated,
He perfects direct knowledge,
Dwells at peace, in that very life,
That sage has crossed beyond all yokes.”

title: “Monks, just as a defiled, dusty cloth, if placed in clean water becomes clean, if placed in a furnace becomes clean. So too, monks, a…
content: “Monks, just as a defiled, dusty cloth, if placed in clean water becomes clean, if placed in a furnace becomes clean. So too, monks, a monk of such virtue, such quality, such wisdom – even if he eats almsfood of choice rice with black grains removed, various soups and curries – that does not become an obstacle for him.”

title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
content: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

title: … (At Sāvatthi). Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: As if struck by a sword,…
content:
… (At Sāvatthi). Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning lust for sensual pleasures.

(The Blessed One):
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning identity view.

title: “Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful…
content: “Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful person; the person who abstains from killing is higher than the killer; the person who abstains from taking what is not given is higher than the taker of what is not given; the person unsmeared by the world, not clinging to personal views, of easy disposition and equanimity, is higher than the person smeared by the world, clinging to personal views, of difficult disposition and lacking equanimity.”

title: Elder Sabbhakāma: This two-footed creature, Impure and foul-smelling, Full of various corpses — From it, fluid oozes. With deer, use a trap; with fish, a…
content:
Elder Sabbhakāma:

This two-footed creature,
Impure and foul-smelling,
Full of various corpses —
From it, fluid oozes.

With deer, use a trap; with fish, a hook;
With monkeys, a pit;
Thus worldlings are caught.

Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, touches —
Agreeable and pleasing —
These five strands of sensual pleasure
Are known in female form.

Worldlings, with mind infatuated,
Run after enjoying female form.
The terrifying cemetery increases,
Storing up renewed existence.

One who avoids female form
As a foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one overcomes
The world’s poisoner.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures,
Security in renunciation,
Having escaped all sensual pleasures,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.
